subject: Learning Methods
title: Self-Explanation in Practice
description: A 60-second lesson on Self-Explanation in Practice.

hook.text: Chi's 1989 study found that students who explained each step of a physics problem to themselves learned twice as fast.

buildup.text: Self-explanation means pausing after each new idea and asking: why does this follow from what came before?

discovery.text: The technique works because it requires inference generation. You must connect ideas, not just read them passively.

twist.text: Poor self-explainers just paraphrase the text. Effective ones ask why and how, bridging to prior knowledge.

climax.text: After reading each paragraph, stop and explain why that information matters and how it connects to what you know.

punchline.text: Don't just restate it. Ask why. That is the key.

quiz.question: What makes self-explanation effective for learning?
options: It requires generating inferences and connecting ideas
